newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Thursday were seen mostly steady-firm, amid outlooks for continued light hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Several hog buyers in Illinois indicated that competition for reduced supplies could underpin prices despite slaughter cutbacks by several packers.
Packers trimmed slaughter operations this week in response to poor pork demand and higher hog prices, they said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota and Illinois top prices for hogs delivered to plants could range $56.00 to $56.50. Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could range $54.00 to $56.50.
"We need help from product prices, we need warmer weather so people will go out and barbecue," a packer buyer said.

Central U.S. carlot pork prices at midday were mixed in slow trading. Fresh loins were not tested, hams were mostly $1.00 per cwt higher, bellies were firm and lean trimmings $1.00 lower, USDA reported.

Slaughter on Wednesday was estimated at 321,000 head, compared with 350,000 last week and 357,000 last year, USDA said. Week to date slaughter was pegged at 946,000 head, down 8.9 percent from a week ago at 1.038 million and down 10.3 percent form a year ago at 1.055 million.
